2. The petitioner's case in short is that the petitioner joined Government service as an Assistant Engineer in the year 1962, being appointed by the then erstwhile Government of East Pakistan on the recommendation of the then Provincial Public Service Commission. The petitioner was promoted to the post of Executive Engineer in the month of June, 1971 and in 1978 he was promoted to the next higher post of Superintending Engineer in Roads and Highways Department and in December, 1982 he was posted as Superintending Engineer, Road. Circle, Dhaka and completed 7(seven) projects in record time as per direction of the then DCMLA and Minister-in-Charge of the Ministry of Communications, Government of Bangladesh. In appreciation of the services of the petitioner the then Chief Engineer, Roads and Highways Department under Memo No. 204-CE dated 5.4.84 addressed to the Secretary, Ministry of Communications, Road, Highways and Road Transport Division recommended the prayer of the petitioner for his encadrement into the Senior Service Pool. After successful completion of seven projects in April, 1984 the petitioner was given the independent. current charge of Additional Engineer, Roads and Highways Department, Dhaka Zone and thereafter he was entrusted with the gigantic task of Road Development of Chittagong Hill Tracts and under a Special 5(five) Years Plan was placed in a newly created post of Additional Chief Engineer under Chittagong Hill Tract Development Board. Because of the quick success of the petitioner in service some of his colleagues became jealous and started sending anonymous letters against the petitioner containing cooked up and false stories of corruption and malpractices against the petitioner to the authorities. On the basis of these false allegations the Secretary of the Ministry of Communication, Roads & Road Transport Division, constituted an Enquiry Committee headed by Mr. Noor Mohammad Akhand, a Joint Secretary of the said Ministry. The committee held enquiry on the back of the petitioner without giving him any opportunity of hearing and prepared a malafide, false and fabricated report against the petitioner. The enquiry committee submitted its report to the Secretary of the Ministry who forwarded the same to the CMLA Secretariat on 1.4.85 where-upon the Secretary called for an explanation from the petitioner as to the allegations in the said report. The petitioner submitted his written defence to the allegation as contained in the said enquiry report. The Secretary perused the written defence of the petitioner against the allegation and thoroughly examined the entire record and found no incriminating materials against the petitioner and accordingly the Secretary sent a report to the CMLA Secretariat under Memo No. EI/7/84-260 dated 19.5.85 stating that there was no material against the petitioner Ibr drawing up of a departmental proceeding. But in the meantime, on the basis of the enquiry report headed by Joint Secretary, the petitioner was dismissed from service with immediate effect under the provisions of MLO No. 9 of 1982 which was communicated to the petitioner as contained in Order No. DS(ENQ)/PA-13/85-240 dated 15.10.85 issued under the signature of the Secretary, Roads and Road Transport Division of the Ministry of Communications of the Government of Bangladesh by order of the President and Chief Martial Law Administrator. It is further stated in the petition that a criminal case was also started against the petitioner by the Co-ordination and Control Cell for National Security as per F.I.R. lodged at Tejgaon P.S. by a Sr. A.S.P.and Deputy Director of the said Cell on 8.1.86 under the provisions of Regulation No. II of the Martial Law Regulation 1 of 1982 which was numbered as Tejgaon P.S. Case No. 113 (1) 86. 

 The petitioner made an application to the CMLA, praying for justice. On the basis of the said application the record of the case was transmitted to the CMLA's Secretariat by the Cordination and Control Cell for National Security after completion of investigation for necessary order for disposal of the case. On examination of the record of the case the said CMLA's Secretariat found the petitioner not guilty to any of the charges and gave the opinion that the criminal case against him should be with-drawn and the dismissal order passed on the petitioner under MLO-9 should be reviewed and rescinded allowing the petitioner reinstatement in service as Addl. Chief Engineer. As per decision taken in the Office of the CMLA's Secretariat, Tejgaon, P.S. Case No. 13(1)86 under Regulation No. II of 1982 vide CMLA's No. 6501/3/ML-2/E./147 dated 1st November, 1986 was withdrawn as per report No. 280 dated 5.11.86. 

 "That with regard to the statement made in para 14 this deponent begs to state that upon an application dated 16.5.86 of the petitioner (vide Annexure 'G') the Secretariat of the Chief Martial Law Administrator processed the same and decided for withdrawal of criminal case against the petitioner and also for his re-instatement in service after rescinding the dismissal order dated 15.10.85 passed under Martial Law Order No. 9 of 1982 vide decision dated 28.10.86 as contained in Annexure 'H'. Accordingly' the petitioner was discharged from the criminal case. But soon after the decision was taken for review of the dismissal order of the petitioner by the CMLA's Secretariat vide Annexure 'H', Martial Law was withdrawn with effect from 10.11.86 by a proclamation of withdrawal of Martial Law dated 10.11.86. With the commencement of the said Proclamation of withdrawal of Martial Law all Proclamation Orders C.M.L.Als Orders, M.L. Regulations, M.L. Orders, and M.L. Instructions were repealed. Thus the Martial Law Order No. 9 of 1982 under which the petition Cr was dismissed and the authority of review there-of provided for was repealed with effect from 10.11.86 the date of commencement of Proclamation of Withdrawal of Martial Law. So, there was no competent authority to pass any order on Review under Article 1A of MLO No. 9 of 1982 for his reinstatement." 

 "The allegation/charges brought against Mr. Ahmed are futile having no substance and they will never end in conviction. There will be miscarriage of justice if Mr. Ahmed is further harassed by prolonging the case. So the case should be disposed of by submitting FRT. Mr. Ahmed has been removed from service on the basis of these frivolous and machinated charges. He would certainly not have been removed from service if real facts (discussed as above) would have been timely mooted and placed before the authority. The said order under MLO-9 should be reviewed and rescinded allowing Mr. Ahmed's prayer for re-instatement in service as Addl. Chief Engineer,"

 21. While the application of the petitioner for review under para '1A' of MLO 9 was pending MLO 9 was repealed by operation of para 2 of the Proclamation of Withdrawal of Martial Law promulgated on 10th November, 1986. Along with its repeal the forum for review and also the right of an aggrieved person to file an application for review under para I A were also abolished and although forum and provision for continuance of pending criminal cases under Martial Law Regulations and Martial Law Orders were made in paras 3 and 4 of the Proclamation of Withdrawal of Martial Law, no provision was made therein or anywhere for disposal of the pending applications for review under para 1A of MLO 9. As a result, two question arise: (I) Whether the right of the petitioner to get the order of his dismissal reviewed subsisted after repeal of MLO 9 and if so, (2) What is the forum for review.
